Pour aider William à faire face à la mal: To help William cope with the disease, a nurse suggests a ritual: drawing himself. Through these self-portraits, he tells of his struggle and gradually reveals the traces of the disease between 1996 and 2001.
Son corps se dégrade, la mémoire dispara: His body deteriorates, memory fades, memories dissolve. His gestures become uncertain and still search for the features of a face that is slowly fading away.
William fera son dernier autoportrait en: William will make his last self-portrait in 2001 and die on 21 March 2007 in London, aged 73.

Entre 1964 et 1966, William Utermohlen p: Between 1964 and 1966, William Utermohlen paints the Dante Cycle, inspired by Dante's Inferno. While 1960s art is optimistic, he chooses a dark, medieval subject to explore suffering and the human condition.
Dans cette série de peintures, William v: In this series of paintings, William set out to explore suffering and the human condition.
L'Enfer de Dante lui permettait de repré: Dante's Inferno let him portray pain, fear and guilt in a dramatic, visual way.
Avec ce cycle, Utermohlen combine un sty: With this cycle, Utermohlen combines a reinterpreted medieval style with a modern sensibility to explore the human condition.

En 1969 William débute une des séries de: In 1969 William begins one of the most disturbing and intriguing series of paintings in his collection.

Musée interactif retraçant la vie de Wil: An interactive museum tracing the life of William Utermohlen, an American painter, and the progression of Alzheimer's disease through his artworks.

William Utermohlen naît le 5 décembre 19: William Utermohlen is born on 5 December 1933 in South Philadelphia, into a family of German immigrants.
Enfant unique, il grandit dans un enviro: An only child, he grows up in a protective environment culturally shaped by European memory.
Au début des années 1950, William voyage: In the early 1950s, William travels through Europe.
C'est là-bas qu'il découvre l'art de la: It is there that he discovers the art of the Italian Renaissance and the French Baroque. These influences will long nourish his attachment to the human figure.
Patricia est l'épouse de William, celle: Patricia is William's wife, the woman who will follow him throughout his life and whom the artist will portray in several portraits. She will be an immense support to him.
En 1962, William s'installe définitiveme: In 1962, William settles permanently in London, where he meets the art historian he will marry in 1965.
Londres devient alors le centre de sa vi: London then becomes the centre of his artistic and personal life, the recurring setting of many portraits and interior scenes
Le diagnostic d'Alzheimer en 1995 et ses: The Alzheimer's diagnosis in 1995 and its first traces in William Utermohlen's work: Blue Skies, portraits of Patricia, faces that fade away.
Après la série d'images \"Conversation\": After the "Conversation" series, William's brain tires. Little by little, he begins to lose control of his body.
Chaque portrait qu'il peindra deviendra: Every portrait he paints will become the silent witness of his dissolving memory.
Après cette annonce, il peint sa dernièr: After this announcement, he paints his last great canvas, Blue Skies (1995). It shows a figure clinging to a table, lost in an empty space. A raw image of the shock that has just upended his life.
Il peint aussi ce portrait, le dernier d: He also paints this portrait, Patricia's last. The features become less and less sure. The colour of her hair no longer reflects reality, and her face appears with exaggerated proportions.
La maladie d'Alzheimer altère peu à peu: Alzheimer's disease gradually impairs his memory and perception, causing confusion, disorientation and anxiety, along with a progressive loss of bearings, autonomy and identity.
